concepts.title: Point Object Approximation
concepts.definition: A simplification where an object is treated as a single mathematical point because its physical size is far less than the distance it shifts.
concepts.key_idea: Object dimensions are ignored when travel distance is significantly large.
question_patterns: can the body be considered a point object
identify if the object is point-like
when is the point object approximation valid
short note on point object approximation
justify why point object approximation matters

solution_steps.explain: evaluate the size of the object against the total path length

solution_steps.action: check the ratio of size to distance
solution_steps.explain: If the object's size is negligible compared to the distance traveled, the point object approximation is valid.
If the size is much smaller than the displacement, treat the object as a point; otherwise the approximation does not hold.

concepts.title: Instantaneous Velocity
concepts.definition: The specific rate of change of an object's position with respect to time at a particular moment.
concepts.key_idea: The tangent's slope to a position-time graph at any specific time.

velocity is the ratio of displacement to time

solution_steps.action: take the limit as the time interval approaches zero
solution_steps.explain: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of the average velocity as the time interval shrinks to zero, giving the derivative dx/dt.

concepts.title: First Equation of Motion
concepts.definition: A kinematic relation that determines the final velocity of an object based on its initial velocity, constant acceleration, and time elapsed.
concepts.key_idea: Velocity increases linearly with time under constant acceleration.
question_patterns: find the final velocity

solution_steps.explain: multiply acceleration by the time elapsed
final velocity is the sum of starting speed and gain

solution_steps.action: round the result to the appropriate significant figures
solution_steps.explain: Round the computed final velocity to match the significant figures of the given initial velocity, acceleration, and time values.

concepts.title: Second Equation of Motion
concepts.definition: A kinematic relation that calculates the displacement of an object under constant acceleration over a specific time.
concepts.key_idea: Displacement is the sum of the distance covered at the initial speed and the extra distance contributed by the acceleration.

solution_steps.explain: multiply starting speed by time

total displacement is the sum of both components

concepts.title: Stopping Distance
concepts.definition: The distance a vehicle travels after brakes are indeed applied before it comes to a complete stop.
concepts.key_idea: Stopping distance grows with the square of the initial velocity.

solution_steps.explain: Round the computed stopping distance to match the least number of significant figures in the given initial velocity and deceleration values.

concepts.title: Relative Velocity
concepts.definition: The velocity of one object as measured from the frame of reference of another moving object.
concepts.key_idea: Velocity is not absolute and varies with the observer's motion.

solution_steps.action: interpret the sign of the result
solution_steps.explain: A positive relative velocity means object A moves ahead of B in the chosen direction; a negative value means A falls behind B.
